evidence: Quint. 1.5.45: in quibus patrium prō possessīvō dīcitur vel contrā
terms.comment: A possessive pronoun or adjective, meus, tuus, suus, is prōnōmen possessīvum or adjectīvum possessīvum (Traupman 233). Quintilian contrasts the possessive adjective with the “paternal” genitive, patrium.

phrases.latin: huic partī subjungātur licet per comparātiōnēs et superlātiōnēs, itemque in quibus patrium prō possessīvō dīcitur vel contrā
phrases.english: to this part one may add mistakes in comparatives and superlatives, and those where the genitive is said for the possessive or the reverse

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 233, p. 248.
